data.zekr: ﴿Inna fi khalqis-samawati wal-ardi wakhtilafil-layli wan-nahari la-ayatil-li-ulil-albab * Alladhina yadhkurunallaha qiyaman wa qu’udan wa ‘ala junubihim wa yatafakkaruna fi khalqis-samawati wal-ard, Rabbana ma khalaqta hadha batilan, subhanaka fa qina ‘adhaban-nar * Rabbana innaka man tudkhilin-nara faqad akhzayta-hu, wa ma lish-zalimeena min ansar * Rabbana innana sami’na munadiyan yunadi lil-imani an aminu bi Rabbikum fa amanna, Rabbana faghfir lana dhunoobana wa kaffir ‘anna sayyi’atina wa tawaffana ma’al-abrar * Rabbana wa atina ma wa’adtana ‘ala rusulika wa la tukhzina yawmal-qiyamah, innaka la tukhliful-mee’ad * Fastajaba lahum Rabbuhum anni la udee’u ‘amala ‘amilim-minkum min dhakarin aw untha, ba’dukum mim ba’d. Falladhina hajaru wa ukhriju min diyarihim wa ouzu fi sabeeli wa qatalu wa qutilu la ukaffiranna ‘anhum sayyi’atihim wa la udkhilannahum jannatin tajri min tahtihal-anhar, thawaban min ‘indillah, wallahu ‘indahu husnut-thawab * La yaghurrannaka taqallubulladhina kafaroo fil-bilad * Mata’un qaleelun thumma ma’wahum jahannamu wa bi’sal-mahad * Lakini-lladhina-ttaqaw Rabbahum lahum jannatun tajri min tahtihal-anhar, khalideena fiha nuzulam-min ‘indillah, wa ma ‘indallahi khayrul-lil-abrar * Wa inna min ahlil-kitabi laman yu’minu billahi wa ma unzila ilaykum wa ma unzila ilayhim, khashi’eena lillah, la yashtaruna bi ayathillahi thamanan qaleelan. Ula’ika lahum ajruhum ‘inda Rabbihim, innallaha saree’ul-hisab * Ya ayyuhalladhina amanu-s-biru wa sabiru wa rabitu wattaqullaha la’allakum tuflihun ﴾.

data.reference:
(1) For the saying of Anas bin Malik - may Allah be pleased with him -: ((It is from the Sunnah, when you enter the mosque, to start with your right foot, and when you exit, to start with your left foot)). Narrated by Al-Hakim, 1/218, and he authenticated it according to the condition of Muslim, and Adh-Dhahabi agreed. And narrated by Al-Bayhaqi, 2/442.
(2) Abu Dawud, no. 466, and see: Sahih Al-Jami’, no. 4591.
(3) Narrated by Ibn As-Sunni, no. 88.

(5) Muslim, 1/494, no. 713. And in the Sunan of Ibn Majah from the narration of Fatimah - may Allah be pleased with her -: ((O Allah, forgive my sins, and open for me the doors of Your mercy)).

data.zekr:
Jabir bin Abdullah - may Allah be pleased with them both - said: The Messenger of Allah - peace be upon him - used to teach us the Istikhara in all matters as he used to teach us a Surah from the Quran. He used to say:
When any one of you is concerned about a matter, he should pray two Rak’ahs other than the obligatory prayer, and then say:
Allahumma inni astakheeruka bi ‘ilmik, wa astaqdiruka bi qudratik, wa as’aluka min fadlikal-‘adheem; fa innaka taqdiru wa la aqdir, wa ta’lamu wa la a’lam, wa Anta ‘allamul-ghuyoob. Allahumma in kunta ta’lamu anna hadhal-amra - and he mentioned his need - khayrun li fi deeni wa ma’ashi wa ‘aaqibati amri - or he said: ‘aajilihi wa aajilih - faqdurhu li wa yassirhu li thumma barik li fih. Wa in kunta ta’lamu anna hadhal-amra shar-run li fi deeni wa ma’ashi wa ‘aaqibati amri - or he said: ‘aajilihi wa aajilih - fasrifhu ‘anni wasrifni ‘anhu, waqdir liyal-khayra haythu kana, thumma ardhini bih(1).

And whoever seeks the choice of the Creator, consults the believing creation, and is firm in his decision, will not regret. Allah the Almighty says: ﴿And consult them in the matter; and when you have decided, then rely upon Allah﴾(2).

data.reference: ((Do not turn your houses into graves. Verily, Satan is repelled from the house in which Surah Al-Baqarah is recited)). Narrated by Muslim, 1/539, no. 780. And among the things that repel Satan are the supplications of morning and evening, sleep and waking, supplications for entering and leaving the house, supplications for entering and leaving the mosque, and other prescribed supplications, such as reciting Ayat Al-Kursi before sleeping, and the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah. And whoever says: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer one hundred times, it will be a protection for him from Satan for his entire day. Likewise, the Adhan repels Satan.

data.reference: ((The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both. Be keen on what benefits you, seek help from Allah and do not be disabled. If something befalls you, do not say: If only I had done so-and-so, it would have been such-and-such. Rather say: Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does, for 'if' opens the door for Satan)). Muslim, 4/2052, no. 2664.
data.zekr: Qadarullahi wa ma sha’a fa’al.

data.category: Congratulating the Newborn and its Response
data.reference:
(1) Mentioned from the words of Al-Hasan Al-Basri. See: Tuhfat Al-Mawdud by Ibn Al-Qayyim, p. 20, and it was attributed to Ibn Al-Mundhir in Al-Awsat.
(2) Said by An-Nawawi in Al-Adhkar, p. 349. And see: Sahih Al-Adhkar of An-Nawawi, by Salim Al-Hilali, 2/713, and the full authentication in Adh-Dhikr wad-Du’a wal-‘Ilaj bir-Ruqa by the author, 1/416.
data.zekr:
Barakallahu laka fil-mawhoobi laka, wa shakarta-l-wahib, wa balagha ushdahu, wa ruziqta birrah(1)
And the one being congratulated replies, saying: Barakallahu laka wa baraka ‘alayk, wa jazakallahu khayran, wa razaqakallahu mithlahu, wa ajzala thawabak(2).

data.category: What to Use to Seek Refuge for Children - Ruqyah
data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 4/119, no. 3371, from the narration of Ibn Abbas - may Allah be pleased with them both -.
data.zekr: The Messenger of Allah - peace be upon him - used to seek refuge for Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn - may Allah be pleased with them both - saying: U’eedhukuma bi kalimati-llahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammah, wa min kulli ‘aynin lammah.

data.category: Supplication When Visiting a Sick Person
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 10/118, no. 3616.
data.zekr: La ba’sa, tuhurun, in sha’Allah.

data.category: Supplication When Visiting a Sick Person
data.reference: ((No Muslim servant visits a sick person whose death has not yet come, and says seven times ... )) the Hadith. ... except that he will recover. Narrated by Tirmidhi, no. 2083, and Abu Dawud, no. 3106. And see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 2/210, and Sahih Al-Jami’, 5/180.
data.zekr: As’alullahal-‘adheema Rabbal-‘Arshil-‘adheem an yashfiyak.

data.reference: Narrated by Tirmidhi, no. 969, and Ibn Majah, no. 1442, and Ahmad, no. 975. And see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 1/244, and Sahih Tirmidhi, 1/286. And also authenticated by Ahmad Shakir.
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - said: ((When a man visits his Muslim brother, he walks in the path of Paradise until he sits down. When he sits down, mercy envelops him. If it is in the morning, seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him until evening. If it is in the evening, seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him until morning)).

data.category: Supplication for a Sick Person Who Has Lost Hope of Life
data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 7/10, no. 4435, and Muslim, 4/1893, no. 2444.
data.zekr: Allahumma-ghfir li, warhamni, wa alhiqni bir-rafeeqil-a’la.

data.category: Supplication for a Sick Person Who Has Lost Hope of Life
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 8/144, no. 4449. The Hadith mentions the use of the Siwak.
data.zekr: At the time of his death, the Prophet - peace be upon him - used to dip his hands in water and wipe his face with them, saying: La ilaha illallahu, inna lil-mawti sakarat.

data.category: Supplication for a Sick Person Who Has Lost Hope of Life
data.reference: Narrated by Tirmidhi, no. 3430, and Ibn Majah, no. 3794.
data.zekr: La ilaha illallahu wallahu Akbar. La ilaha illallahu wahdahu. La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah. La ilaha illallahu lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd. La ilaha illallahu wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

data.reference: Abu Dawud, 3/190, no. 3116, and see: Sahih Al-Jami’, 5/432.
data.zekr: Whoever’s last words are: La ilaha illallah, will enter Paradise.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Suffers a Calamity
data.reference: Muslim, 2/632, no. 918.
data.zekr: Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’oon. Allahumma-jurni fi museebati, wa-khlif li khayran minha.

data.category: Supplication When Closing the Eyes of the Deceased
data.reference: Muslim, 2/634, no. 920.
data.zekr: Allahumma-ghfir li Fulani (mention his name), warfa’ darajatahu fil-mahdiyyeen, wakh-lufhu fi ‘aqibihi fil-ghabireen, waghfir lana wa lahu ya Rabbal-‘alamin. Wafsah lahu fi qabrihi, wa nawwir lahu fih.

data.category: Supplication for the Deceased in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: Muslim, 2/663, no. 963.
data.zekr: Allahumma-ghfir lahu, warhamhu, wa ‘aafih, wa-’fu ‘anhu, wa akrim nuzulahu, wa wassi’ mudkhalahu, waghsilhu bil-maa’i wath-thalji wal-barad. Wa naqqihi minal-khataya kama naqqaytas-thawbal-abyada minad-danas. Wa abdilhu daaran khayran min daarih, wa ahlan khayran min ahlih, wa zawjan khayran min zawjih. Wa adkhilhul-jannah, wa a’idh-hu min ‘adhabil-qabr [wa ‘adhabin-nar].

data.category: Supplication for the Deceased in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: Abu Dawud, no. 3201, Tirmidhi, no. 1024, An-Nasa’i, no. 1985, Ibn Majah, 1/480, no. 1498, and Ahmad, 2/368, no. 8809. And see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 1/251.
data.zekr: Allahumma-ghfir li hayyina wa mayyitina, wa shahidina wa ghaa’ibina, wa sagheerina wa kabeerina, wa dhakarinna wa unthaana. Allahumma man ahyaytahu minna fa-ahyihi ‘alal-Islam, wa man tawaffaytahu minna fa-tawaffahu ‘alal-iman. Allahumma la tahrimna ajrahu, wa la tudhillana ba’dah.

data.category: Supplication for the Deceased in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: Narrated by Ibn Majah, no. 1499. See: Sahih Ibn Majah, 1/251. And narrated by Abu Dawud, 3/211, no. 3202.
data.zekr: Allahumma inna Fulana-bna Fulani fi dhimmatika, wa habl-i-jiwarik, faqihi min fitnatil-qabr, wa ‘adhabin-nar, wa Anta ahlul-wafa’i wal-haqq. Fagfir lahu warhamhu, innaka Antal-Ghafoorur-Raheem.

data.category: Supplication for the Deceased in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: Narrated by Al-Hakim, who authenticated it and Adh-Dhahabi agreed, 1/359.
data.zekr: Allahumma ‘abdunka wa-bnu amatika, ihtaja ila rahmatik, wa Anta ghaniyyun ‘an ‘adhabih. In kana muhsinan fa-zid fi hasanatih, wa in kana musee’an fa-tajawaz ‘anh.

data.category: Supplication for a Pre-born Child in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: ((Saeed bin Al-Musayyib said: I prayed behind Abu Hurayrah for a child who had not committed any sin. So I heard him say ... )) the Hadith. Narrated by Malik in Al-Muwatta, 1/288, and Ibn Abi Shaybah in Al-Musannaf, 3/217, and Al-Bayhaqi, 4/9. And its chain of narration was authenticated by Shu’ayb Al-Arna’ut in his verification of Sharh As-Sunnah by Al-Baghawi, 5/357.
data.zekr: Allahumma a’idh-hu min ‘adhabil-qabr. And if he says: Allahumma-j’alhu faratan wa dhukhran li-walidayh, wa shafi’an mujaban. Allahumma thaqqil bihi mawazeenahuma, wa a’dhim bihi ujurahoma, wa alhiq-hu bi salihil-mu’mineen, wa-j’alhu fi kafaalati Ibrahim, wa qihi bi rahmatika ‘adhabal-jaheem, wa abdilhu daaran khayran min daarih, wa ahlan khayran min ahlih. Allahumma-ghfir li aslaafina, wa afraatina, wa man sabaqana bil-iman. If he says this, it is good.

data.category: Supplication for a Pre-born Child in the Funeral Prayer
data.reference: See: Al-Mughni by Ibn Qudamah, 3/416.
data.zekr: Allahumma-j’alhu lana faratan, wa salafan, wa ajran.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 2/80, no. 1284, and Muslim, 2/636, no. 923.
data.zekr: Innallaha akhadha, wa lahu ma a’ta, wa kullu shay’in ‘indahu bi ajalim-musamma. Fal-tasbir wal-tahtasib. And if he says: A’dhamallahu ajrak, wa ahsana ‘azaa’ak, wa ghafara li-mayyitik, then it is good.

data.category: Supplication When Placing the Deceased in the Grave
data.reference: Abu Dawud, 3/314, no. 3215, with a Sahih chain of narration, and Ahmad, no. 5234, and no. 4812 with the wording: ((Bismillah, and upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah)), and its chain of narration is Sahih.
data.zekr: Bismillahi wa ‘ala sunnati Rasoolillah.

data.reference: The Prophet - peace be upon him - when he finished burying the deceased, would stand over him and say: ((Ask Allah to forgive your brother, and ask Allah to grant him steadfastness, for he is being questioned now)). Abu Dawud, 3/315, no. 3223, and Al-Hakim, who authenticated it and Adh-Dhahabi agreed, 1/370.
data.zekr: Allahumma-ghfir lahu, Allahumma-thabbit-hu.

data.reference: Muslim, 2/671, no. 975, and Ibn Majah, 1/494, and the wording is from him, no. 1547 from the narration of Buraydah - may Allah be pleased with him -. And what is between the parentheses is an addition from the narration of Aisha - may Allah be pleased with her - in Muslim, 2/671, no. 975.
data.zekr: As-salamu ‘alaykum ahlad-diyar, minal-mu’mineena wal-muslimeen, wa inna in sha’allahu bikum laahiqoon, [wa yarhamullahu-l-mustaqdimeena minna wal-musta’khireen]. As’alullaha lana wa lakumul-‘aafiyah.

data.reference: Narrated by Abu Dawud, 4/326, no. 5099, and Ibn Majah, 2/1228, no. 3727, and see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 2/305.
data.zekr: Allahumma inni as’aluka khayraha, wa a’udhu bika min sharriha.

data.reference: Muslim, and the wording is from him, 2/666, no. 899, and Al-Bukhari, 4/76, no. 3206, 4829.
data.zekr: Allahumma inni as’aluka khayraha, wa khayra ma fiha, wa khayra ma ursilat bihi, wa a’udhu bika min sharriha, wa sharri ma fiha, wa sharri ma ursilat bihi.

data.reference: Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr - may Allah be pleased with them both - when he heard thunder, he would stop talking and say: ... the Hadith. Al-Muwatta, 2/992.
data.zekr: Subhanalladhi yusabbihur-ra’du bi hamdihi wal-mala’ikatu min kheefatih.

data.reference: Abu Dawud, 1/303, no. 1171.
data.zekr: Allahumma-sqina ghaythan mughithan maree’an maree’an, naafi’an ghayra dhaar, ‘aajilan ghayra aajil.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 1/224, no. 1014, and Muslim, 2/613, no. 897.
data.zekr: Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna, Allahumma aghithna.

data.reference: Abu Dawud, 1/305, no. 1178.
data.zekr: Allahumma-sqi ‘ibadaka, wa bahaa’imaka, wan-shur rahmataka, wa ahyi baladakal-mayyit.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 2/518, no. 1032.
data.zekr: Allahumma sayyiban naafi’an.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 2/518, no. 1032.
data.zekr: Mutirna bi fadlillahi wa rahmatik.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 1/224, no. 933, and Muslim, 2/614, no. 897.
data.zekr: Allahumma hawalayna wa la ‘alayna. Allahumma ‘alal-aakaami wadh-dhiraab, wa butoonil-awdiyah, wa manaabitish-shajar.

data.category: Supplication Upon Seeing the New Moon
data.reference: Tirmidhi, 5/504, no. 3451, and Ad-Darimi with its wording, 1/336, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/157.
data.zekr: Allahu Akbar. Allahumma ahil-hu ‘alayna bil-amni wal-iman, was-salaamati wal-Islam, wat-tawfeeqi lima tuhibbu Rabbana wa tardha. Rabbuna wa Rabbukallahu.

data.reference: Narrated by Abu Dawud, 2/306, no. 2359, and others. And see: Sahih Al-Jami’, 4/209.
data.zekr: Dhahabadh-dhama’u, wabtallatil-‘urooq, wa thabatil-ajru, in sha’Allah.

data.reference: Narrated by Ibn Majah, 1/557, no. 1753, from the supplication of Abdullah bin Amr - may Allah be pleased with him -. And Al-Hafiz authenticated it in the verification of Al-Adhkar. See: Sharh Al-Adhkar, 4/342.
data.zekr: Allahumma inni as’aluka bi rahmatikallati wasi’at kulla shay’in an taghfira li.

data.reference: Narrated by Abu Dawud, 3/347, no. 3767, and Tirmidhi, 4/288, no. 1858, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 2/167.
data.zekr: When any one of you eats food, let him say: Bismillah. If he forgets at the beginning, let him say: Bismillah at the beginning and at the end.

data.reference: Tirmidhi, 5/506, no. 3455, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/158.
data.zekr: Whoever Allah feeds food, let him say: Allahumma barik lana fihi wa at’imna khayran minhu. And whoever Allah gives milk to drink, let him say: Allahumma barik lana fihi wa zidna minhu.

data.reference: Narrated by the compilers of Sunan except An-Nasa’i: Abu Dawud, no. 4025, Tirmidhi, no. 3458, and Ibn Majah, no. 3285. And see Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/159.
data.zekr: Al-hamdu lillahilladhi at’amani hadha, wa razaqanihi, min ghayri hawlim-minni wa la quwwah.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 6/214, no. 5458, and Tirmidhi with its wording, 5/507, no. 3456.
data.zekr: Al-hamdu lillahi hamdan katheeran tayyiban mubarakan fih, ghayra [makfiyyin wa la] muwadda’in, wa la mustaghna ‘anhu Rabbana.

data.category: Supplication of the Guest for the Host
data.zekr: Allahumma barik lahum fima razaqtahum, waghfir lahum warhamhum.

data.category: Indirect Supplication for Food or Drink
data.zekr: Allahumma at’im man at’amani, wasqi man saqaani.

data.category: Supplication When Breaking Fast at a Household
data.reference: Sunan Abu Dawud, 3/367, no. 3856, and Ibn Majah, 1/556, no. 1747, and An-Nasa’i in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, no. 296-298. It is stated that he - peace be upon him - used to say this when breaking fast at a household.
data.zekr: Aftara ‘indakmus-saa’imoona, wa akala ta’aamakal-abraaru, wa salla ‘alaykumul-malaa’ikah.

data.category: Supplication of the Fasting Person When Food is Presented and He is Not Breaking Fast
data.zekr: When one of you is invited, he should accept. If he is fasting, he should pray, and if he is not fasting, he should eat. And the meaning of 'he should pray' is 'he should supplicate'.

data.category: What to Say When Someone Insults the Fasting Person
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 4/103, no. 1894, and Muslim, 2/806, no. 1151.
data.zekr: Inni saa’im, inni saa’im.

data.category: Supplication Upon Seeing the First Fruits
data.zekr: Allahumma barik lana fi thamarina, wa barik lana fi madeenatina, wa barik lana fi saa’ina, wa barik lana fi muddina.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 7/125, no. 5870.
data.zekr: When one of you sneezes, he should say: Al-hamdu lillah. And his brother or companion should say to him: Yarhamukallah. And when he says to him: Yarhamukallah, he should say: Yahdeekumullahu wa yuslihu balakum.

data.category: What to Say to a Non-Muslim Who Sneezes and Praises Allah
data.reference: Tirmidhi, 5/82, no. 2741, and Ahmad, 4/400, no. 19586, and Abu Dawud, 4/308, no. 5040. And see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 2/354.
data.zekr: Yahdeekumullahu wa yuslihu balakum.

data.reference: Narrated by the compilers of Sunan except An-Nasa’i: Abu Dawud, no. 2130, Tirmidhi, no. 1091, Ibn Majah, no. 1905, and An-Nasa’i in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, no. 259. And see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 1/316.
data.zekr: Barakallahu laka, wa baraka ‘alayk, wa jama’a baynakuma fi khayr.

data.category: Supplication for the Newly Married and When Buying an Animal
data.reference: Abu Dawud, 2/248, no. 2160, and Ibn Majah, 1/617, no. 1918, and see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 1/324.
data.zekr: When one of you marries a woman, or buys a servant, let him say: Allahumma inni as’aluka khayraha, wa khayra ma jabaltaha ‘alayh, wa a’udhu bika min sharriha, wa sharri ma jabaltaha ‘alayh. And when he buys a camel, let him take it by the hump of its neck and say the same.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 6/141, no. 141, and Muslim, 2/1028, no. 1434.
data.zekr: Bismillah, Allahumma jannibnash-shaytana, wa jannibish-shaytana ma razaqtana.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari, 7/99, no. 3282, and Muslim, 4/2015, no. 2610.
data.zekr: A’udhu billahish-shaytanir-rajeem.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Sees an Afflicted Person
data.reference: Tirmidhi, 5/494, 5/493, no. 3432, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/153.
data.zekr: Al-hamdu lillahilladhi ‘aafani mimma ibtalaka bih, wa fadhalani ‘ala katheermimman khalaqa tafdeela.

data.category: What to Say in a Gathering
data.reference: Tirmidhi, no. 3434, and Ibn Majah, no. 3814, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/153, and Sahih Ibn Majah, 2/321. The wording is from Tirmidhi.
data.zekr: From Abdullah bin Amr - may Allah be pleased with them both - who said: It was counted that the Messenger of Allah - peace be upon him - used to say in one sitting: Rabbi-ghfir li, wa tub ‘alayya, innaka Antat-Tawwab-ul-Ghafoor, one hundred times before he stood up.

data.reference: The compilers of Sunan: Abu Dawud, no. 4858, Tirmidhi, no. 3433, An-Nasa’i, no. 1344. And see Sahih Tirmidhi 3/153. It is also narrated that Aisha - may Allah be pleased with her - said: ((The Messenger of Allah - peace be upon him - never sat in a gathering, nor recited the Quran, nor prayed a prayer, except that he concluded it with these words ... )) the Hadith. Narrated by An-Nasa’i in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, no. 308, and Ahmad, 6/77, no. 24486.
data.zekr: Subhanakallahumma wa bihamdik, ash-hadu an la ilaha illa Ant, astaghfiruka wa atubu ilayk.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Says 'May Allah Forgive You'
data.reference: Ahmad, 5/82, no. 20778, and An-Nasa’i in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, p. 218, no. 421.
data.zekr: Wa laka.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Does a Favor for You
data.reference: Narrated by Tirmidhi, no. 2035, and see: Sahih Al-Jami’, 6244, and Sahih Tirmidhi, 2/200.
data.zekr: Jazakallahu khayran.

data.reference: Muslim, 1/555, no. 809. And in another narration: from the end of Surah Al-Kahf, 1/556, no. 809.
data.zekr: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal. And seeking refuge in Allah from his trials after the final Tashahhud of every prayer.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Says 'I Love You for the Sake of Allah'

data.zekr: Ahabba kal-ladhi ahbabtani lah.

data.zekr: Barakallahu laka fi ahlika wa malik.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Lends When Repaying
data.reference: Narrated by An-Nasa’i in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, p. 300, and Ibn Majah, 2/809, no. 2424. And see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 2/55.
data.zekr: Barakallahu laka fi ahlika wa malik. Innama jazaa’us-salafi-l-hamdu wal-adaa’.

data.reference: Ahmad, 4/403, no. 19606, and Al-Adab Al-Mufrad of Al-Bukhari, no. 716. And see: Sahih Al-Jami’, 3/233.
data.zekr: Allahumma inni a’udhu bika an ushrika bika wa ana a’lam, wa astaghfiruka lima la a’lam.

data.category: Supplication for One Who Says 'May Allah Bless You'
data.reference: Narrated by Ibn As-Sunni in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, p. 138, no. 278. And see: Al-Wabil As-Sayyib of Ibn Al-Qayyim, p. 304.
data.zekr: Wa fika barakallahu.

data.reference: Ahmad, 2/220, no. 7045, and Ibn As-Sunni, no. 292. As for good omens, the Prophet - peace be upon him - used to like them. Therefore, he heard a good word from a man that pleased him, so he said: ((We have taken your good omen from your mouth)). Abu Dawud, no. 3719, and Ahmad, no. 9040.
data.zekr: Allahumma la tayra illa tayruk, wa la khayra illa khayruk, wa la ilaha ghayruk.

data.reference: Abu Dawud, 3/34, no. 2602, and Tirmidhi, 5/501, no. 3446, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/156. The two verses are from Surah Az-Zukhruf: 13-14.
data.zekr: Bismillah, wal-hamdu lillah. ﴿Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrineen, wa inna ila Rabbina la munqaliboon﴾. Al-hamdu lillah, Al-hamdu lillah, Al-hamdu lillah. Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. Subhanakallahumma inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li; fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunooba illa Ant.

Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar. ﴿Subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrineen * Wa inna ila Rabbina la munqaliboon﴾. Allahumma inna nas’aluka fi safarina hadhal-birra wat-taqwa, wa minal-‘amali ma tardha. Allahumma hawwin ‘alayna safarana hadha watwi ‘anna bu’dah. Allahumma Antas-saheebu fis-safari, wal-khaleefatu fil-ahli. Allahumma inni a’udhu bika min wa’tha’is-safari, wa ka’abatil-mandhari, wa soo’il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahli. And when he returned, he would say these words and add to them: Aa’iboona, taa’iboona, ‘aabidoona, li Rabbina haamidoon.

data.category: Supplication for Entering a Village or Town
data.reference: Al-Hakim, who authenticated it and Adh-Dhahabi agreed, 2/100, and Ibn As-Sunni, no. 524. Al-Hafiz authenticated its chain of narration in Takhrīj Al-Adhkar, 5/154.
data.zekr: Allahumma Rabba-s-samawati-s-sab’i wa ma adhlalna, wa Rabba-l-aradeenis-sab’i wa ma aqlalna, wa Rabba-sh-shayateeni wa ma adhlalna, wa Rabbar-riyah wa ma dharayna. data.reference: Tirmidhi, no. 3428, and Ibn Majah, 5/291, no. 3860, and Al-Hakim, 1/538.
data.zekr: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku, wa lahul-hamdu, yuhyi wa yumeetu, wa Huwa Hayyun la yamoot, biyadil-khayr, wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer.

data.zekr: Bismillah.

data.reference: Ahmad, 2/403, no. 9230, and Ibn Majah, 2/943, no. 2825. And see: Sahih Ibn Majah, 2/133.
data.zekr: Astawdi’ukumullahal-ladhi la tadhee’u wadaa’i’uh.

data.category: Supplication of the Resident for the Traveler
data.reference: Ahmad, 2/7, no. 4524, and Tirmidhi, 5/499, no. 3443.
data.zekr: Astawdi’ullaha deenaka, wa amaanataka, wa khawaateema ‘amalik.

data.category: Supplication of the Resident for the Traveler
data.reference: Tirmidhi, no. 3444, and see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/155.
data.zekr: Zawwada-kal-lahut-taqwa, wa ghafara dhanbak, wa yassara lakal-khayra haythu ma kunt.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 6/135, no. 2993.
data.zekr: Jabir - may Allah be pleased with him - said: When we ascended, we would say Allahu Akbar, and when we descended, we would say Subhanallah.

data.category: Supplication of the Traveler at Dawn
data.reference: Muslim, 4/2086, no. 2718. And the meaning of 'Sami’a saami’un' is: a witness has testified to Allah’s praise for His blessings and His good trials upon us. And the meaning of 'Samm’a saami’un' is: let a witness convey what I say to others, and say the same to remind of remembrance at dawn and supplication. See: Sharh An-Nawawi ‘ala Sahih Muslim, 17/39.
data.zekr: Sami’a saami’un bi hamdillah, wa husni balaa’ihi ‘alayna. Rabbana saahibna, wa afdhil ‘alayna, ‘aa’idhan billahi minan-nar.

data.category: Supplication When Stopping at a Place During Travel or Otherwise
data.zekr: A’udhu bi kalimati-llahit-tammati min sharri ma khalaq.

data.reference: The Prophet - peace be upon him - used to say this when returning from a Ghazwah or Hajj. Al-Bukhari, 7/163, no. 1797, and Muslim, 2/980, no. 1344.
data.zekr: He would say Allahu Akbar on every high ground three times, then say: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku, wa lahul-hamdu, wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer. Aa’iboona, taa’iboona, ‘aabidoona, li Rabbina haamidoon. Sadaqal-lahu wa’dah, wa nasara ‘abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaaba wahdah.

data.category: What to Say When Something Pleasing or Displeasing Happens
data.reference: Narrated by Ibn As-Sunni in ‘Amal Al-Yawm wal-Laylah, no. 377, and Al-Hakim, who authenticated it, 1/499.
data.zekr: When the Prophet - peace be upon him - received something that pleased him, he would say: Al-hamdu lillahilladhi bi ni’matihi tatimmus-saalihaat. And when he received something that displeased him, he would say: Al-hamdu lillahi ‘ala kulli haal.

data.category: Virtue of Sending Blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
data.reference: Narrated by Muslim, 1/288, no. 384.
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - said: ((Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times)).

data.category: Virtue of Sending Blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
data.reference: Abu Dawud, 2/218, no. 2044, and Ahmad, 2/367, no. 8804.
data.zekr: And he said - peace be upon him -: ((Do not make my grave a place of festival, but send blessings upon me, for your blessings reach me wherever you are)).

data.category: Virtue of Sending Blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
data.reference: Tirmidhi, 5/551, no. 3546, and others. And see: Sahih Al-Jami’, 3/25, and Sahih Tirmidhi, 3/177.
data.zekr: And he said - peace be upon him -: ((The miser is the one who remembers me in his presence and does not send blessings upon me)).

data.category: Virtue of Sending Blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
data.reference: An-Nasa’i, 3/43, no. 1282, and Al-Hakim, 2/421.
data.zekr: And he said - peace be upon him -: ((Allah has angels who travel the earth, conveying to me the greetings of my Ummah)).

data.category: Virtue of Sending Blessings on the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
data.reference: Abu Dawud, no. 2041.
data.zekr: And he said - peace be upon him -: ((There is no one who sends greetings upon me except that Allah returns my soul to me so that I may return his greeting)).

data.reference: Muslim, 1/74, no. 54, and Ahmad, no. 1430. The wording is from Ahmad. And the wording of Muslim is: ((You will not enter ... )).
data.zekr: The Messenger of Allah - peace be upon him - said: ((You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread Salam among yourselves)).

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 1/82, no. 28, from the narration of Ammar - may Allah be pleased with him - in a suspended form.
data.zekr: Three things, whoever possesses them, possesses faith: being just with yourself, spreading Salam to everyone, and spending in times of poverty.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 1/55, no. 12, and Muslim, 1/65, no. 39.
data.zekr: And from Abdullah bin Umar - may Allah be pleased with them both -: A man asked the Prophet - peace be upon him -: Which aspect of Islam is best? He said: ((Feeding food, and saying Salam to those whom you know and those whom you do not know)).

data.category: How to Respond to a Non-Muslim's Salam
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 11/42, no. 6258, and Muslim, 4/1705, no. 2163.
data.zekr: If the People of the Book greet you, say: Wa ‘alaykum.

data.category: Supplication Upon Hearing the Crowing of a Rooster and the Braying of a Donkey
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 6/350, no. 3303, and Muslim, 4/2092, no. 2729.
data.zekr: When you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah from His bounty, for they have seen an angel. And when you hear the braying of donkeys, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for they have seen a devil.

data.category: Supplication Upon Hearing the Barking of Dogs at Night
data.reference: Abu Dawud, 4/327, no. 5105, and Ahmad, 3/306, no. 14283.
data.zekr: When you hear the barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys at night, seek refuge in Allah from them, for they see what you do not see.

data.category: What to Say to One Who Has Cursed You
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 11/171, no. 6361, and Muslim, 4/2007, no. 396. The wording is: ((Then make it a purification and mercy for him)).
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - said: ((O Allah, if I have cursed any believer, then make that a means of drawing him closer to You on the Day of Resurrection)).

data.category: What a Muslim Should Say When Praising Another Muslim
data.reference: Narrated by Muslim, 4/2296, no. 3000.
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - said: ((If one of you is to praise his brother without fail, he should say: I consider so-and-so to be so-and-so, and Allah is his Reckoner. I do not purify anyone over Allah. I consider him - if he knows that - to be such-and-such)).

data.category: What a Muslim Should Say When Praised
data.reference: Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, no. 761. What is between the parentheses is an addition from Al-Bayhaqi in Shu’ab Al-Iman, 4/228, from another chain of narration.
data.zekr: Allahumma la tu’akhidhni bima yaqooloon, waghfir li ma la ya’lamoon, [wa-j’alni khayram mimma yadhunnoon].

data.category: How Should the Muhrim Recite the Talbiyah During Hajj or Umrah?
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 3/408, no. 1549, and Muslim, 2/841, no. 1184.
data.zekr: Labbaykallahumma labbayk, labbayka la shareeka laka labbayk, innal-hamda, wan-ni’mata, laka wal-mulk, la shareeka lak.

data.category: Tahlil When Reaching the Black Stone
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 3/476, no. 1613. And the meaning of 'shay' (thing) is: a crook. See: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 3/472.
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - performed Tawaf around the House on a camel. Whenever he reached the corner, he would point to it with something he had and say Allahu Akbar.

data.category: Supplication Between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone
data.reference: Abu Dawud, 2/179, no. 1894, and Ahmad, 3/411, no. 15398, and Al-Baghawi in Sharh As-Sunnah, 7/128. And the verse is from Surah Al-Baqarah: 201.
data.zekr: ﴿Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina ‘adhaban-nar﴾.

data.category: Supplication When Standing on Safa and Marwah
data.reference: Muslim, 2/888, no. 1218. And the verse is from Surah Al-Baqarah, no. 158.
data.zekr: When the Prophet - peace be upon him - approached Safa, he recited: ﴿Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾. I begin with what Allah began with. So he began with Safa and ascended it until he saw the House. He faced the Qiblah, then declared the Oneness of Allah and magnified Him, and said: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer. La ilaha illallahu wahdah, anjaza wa’dah, wa nasara ‘abdah, wa hazamal-ahzaaba wahdah. Then he supplicated between these words. He said the same three times. The Hadith continues, and it mentions that he did on Marwah what he did on Safa.

data.category: Supplication on the Day of Arafah
data.reference: Tirmidhi, no. 3585.
data.zekr: The Prophet - peace be upon him - said: ((The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of Arafah, and the best of what I and the Prophets before me have said is: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la shareeka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa Huwa ‘ala kulli shay’in qadeer)).

The Prophet - peace be upon him - rode Al-Qaswa’ until he reached Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram. He faced the Qiblah (and supplicated to Him, magnified Him, declared His Oneness, and affirmed His uniqueness). He remained standing until dawn broke clearly, then he departed before sunrise.

data.category: Tahlil When Throwing Pebbles at the Jamarat with Each Pebble
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 3/583, no. 1751, and see its wording there. And Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 3/583, 3/584, 3/581, no. 1753. And Muslim also narrated it, no. 1218.
data.zekr: He says Allahu Akbar each time he throws a pebble at the three Jamarat, then he moves forward and stands, supplicating facing the Qiblah, raising his hands after the first and second Jamarah. As for the Jamrat Al-Aqabah, he throws it and says Allahu Akbar with each pebble, then he departs and does not stand at it.

data.category: Supplication for Astonishment and Good News
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 1/210, 390, 414, no. 115, 3599, 6218, and Muslim, 4/1857, no. 1674.
data.zekr: Subhanallah!.

data.category: Supplication for Astonishment and Good News
data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 8/441, no. 4741, and no. 3062, Tirmidhi, no. 2180, An-Nasa’i in Al-Kubra, no. 11185. And see: Sahih Tirmidhi, 2/103, 2/235, and Musnad Ahmad, 5/218, no. 21900.
data.zekr: Allahu Akbar!.

data.category: What to Do When Something Pleasing Happens
data.reference: Narrated by the compilers of Sunan except An-Nasa’i: Abu Dawud, no. 2774, Tirmidhi, no. 1578, and Ibn Majah, no. 1394. See Sahih Ibn Majah, 1/233.
data.zekr: When the Prophet - peace be upon him - received something that pleased him or made him happy, he would fall prostrate in gratitude to Allah the Blessed and Exalted.

data.category: What to Say When Feeling Pain in the Body
data.zekr: Place your hand on the part of your body that hurts and say: Bismillah, three times. And say seven times: A’udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhir.

data.category: Supplication for Fear of the Evil Eye
data.reference: Musnad Ahmad 4/447, no. 15700, and Ibn Majah, no. 3508, and Malik, 3/118-119. And see the verification of Zad Al-Ma’ad by Al-Arna’ut 4/170.
data.zekr: When one of you sees something in his brother, or in himself, or in his wealth that he admires [let him supplicate for blessings for him], for the evil eye is real.

data.reference: Al-Bukhari with Al-Fath, 6/381, no. 3346, and Muslim, 4/2208, no. 2880.
data.zekr: La ilaha illallah.

data.category: What to Say When Slaughtering or Sacrificing
data.reference: Muslim, 3/1557, no. 196
